newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi prince in talks with Lonrho.
newsitem.headline: Saudi prince in talks with Lonrho.

text.p: Saudi billionaire investor Prince al-Waleed bin Talal is negotiating the purchase of British conglomerate Lonrho Plc's Princess hotels for $300 million, financial sources said on Monday.
"He is the only bidder and has exclusive rights to negotiate the purchase. The price is $300 million," one of the sources told Reuters in Dubai by telephone.

But the financial sources said Lonrho's chief executive Dieter Bock was expected to arrive in the Saudi capital Riyadh, headquarters of the prince's Kingdom Establishment business empire, on Tuesday for discussions.

Prince Waleed has substantial investments in Citicorp, Euro Disney SCA, Canary Wharf in London's docklands, U.S. retail group Saks Fifth Avenue, the Plaza Hotel in New York and the Four Seasons and Fairmont Hotel chains.

Lonrho said in September it had received expressions of interest from potential buyers for its British Metropole chain and the Princess chain of five-star resort hotels and was delaying the planned flotation of the properties.
It said both British and overseas parties had expressed interest in the hotels, with some looking at the entire group and others interested in parts of it.
The Princess hotels include resorts in Acapulco, Mexico, the Caribbean and the United States.
The Metropole, which has five locations in London, Birmingham, Brighton and Blackpool, is a four-star chain with extensive conference facilities.
Some analysts said the hotels would command a premium to the estimated market valuation. But others said Lonhro might be willing to sell at a price close to the market value in order to avoid risk.
Analysts have estimated that a public offering of the Metropole and Princess hotels would bring a market valuation of about 700 million pounds ($1.1 billion).
Britain's Sunday Telegraph newspaper said Prince Waleed was poised to "clinch his position as favourite bidder" for the Princess hotels.
